title: How a Train Services a Customer
description: The portfolio demo as the AI would send it. Track and facility lengths are illustrative; the original drawing has none.

arrival.text: A local train arrives on the main line with the customer's loaded cars.

work.text: The locomotive shoves the loaded cars through the turnout and spots them at the unloading racks.
The locomotive cuts off, leaving the loaded cars at the facility.
It pulls back out through the turnout and leaves for other work.
While the locomotive is away, the customer unloads the cars.
Later, the locomotive returns, running back in through the turnout to the empty cars.
It pulls them back out onto the main line.

departure.text: The train departs with the empties. The customer is served, ready for the next cycle.

questions.ask: How long is the customer siding? It isn't labelled.
questions.basis: Drawn at a bit over half the width of the main line.

questions.ask: How much track do the unloading racks cover?
questions.basis: The racks box covers about half the siding; 5 cars at 66 ft is 330 ft.

questions.ask: Does the train leave westbound, back the way it came?
questions.basis: Step 7 shows the train heading back toward the left edge.
